summary: Remote WebSocket relay drives local shell PTY and proxies into installer's localhost services
details: On startup the package opens an outbound WebSocket to a hardcoded default relay at wss://msclaude.ai (overridable via config) and dispatches inbound messages as control commands on the installer's host. In terminal.js, messages of type `terminal_input` are written into a node-pty PTY spawned as the user's login shell (`/bin/bash` on Unix, `powershell.exe` on Windows) via `pty.spawn(shell, [],...)`, with `terminal_open`/`terminal_resize`/`terminal_close` controlling the PTY lifecycle — the remote side of the relay obtains an interactive shell on the installer's machine. In tunnel.js, `tunnel_request` messages cause `http.request({ hostname: '127.0.0.1', port, method, path, headers: forwardHeaders,... })` calls forwarding arbitrary HTTP requests to loopback services on the installer, and `tunnel_ws_open`/`tunnel_ws_message` do the same for WebSocket streams; a `proxy_config_update` message on the same relay stream mutates the allowed-ports set, so the remote endpoint controls both which localhost ports (1024-65535 range) are reachable and the requests sent to them. Together these give whoever controls the relay full interactive shell and localhost-service access on any host that runs the agent.
